source.title: Bible Atlas
source.source_scope: Uploaded Bible Atlas used to extract chapter structure, map titles, historical-geographical periods, and study indexing.
source.rights_status: Reuse licence not stated in the uploaded PDF.
source.display_policy: Do not redistribute the atlas map images from this dataset. Logos uses derived factual/index metadata and page references only until image reuse rights are verified.

method_note: The atlas itself emphasizes that biblical geography should be studied historically, showing physical geography, changing empires and place names, and archaeological evidence that illuminates and supplements the biblical text. Logos uses this dataset as a historical-geographical index, not as a replacement for Scripture or for current archaeological scholarship.

passage_rules.label: Roman imperial and early Christian setting
Early Persian-period Jerusalem and Yehud during temple restoration

historical_context.setting: Jerusalem and Yehud under Achaemenid Persian rule during the rebuilding of the Second Temple.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: For Zechariah 1:15, the text speaks of 'the nations that are at ease' without supplying an exhaustive list. The map therefore shows the regional and imperial setting rather than claiming that every displayed region is a direct referent of the verse.
historical_context.source_basis: Bible Atlas chapter 13: The Persian Period, especially the Persian Empire, return to Judah, and post-exilic Palestine.

topics.title: World Powers of the 6th century BCE
The Return of the Jewish Exiles to Judah

passage_rules.label: Later prophetic oracles centered on Jerusalem and the surrounding lands

historical_context.setting: Jerusalem remains the literary-geographical center, but the precise compositional setting of Zechariah 9–14 is debated.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: The map provides geographic orientation only. It does not use a disputed date or political reconstruction as though it were certain.
historical_context.source_basis: Bible Atlas post-exilic and Persian-period geography provides the base geographic frame.

passage_rules.label: Jerusalem and Yehud during the rebuilding of the Second Temple

historical_context.setting: Jerusalem/Yehud under Persian rule during the temple-rebuilding campaign associated with Zerubbabel and Joshua.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: The geographic focus is deliberately narrow because Haggai is strongly centered on Jerusalem, the temple, and the restored community.
historical_context.source_basis: Bible Atlas chapter 13: Persian-period Judah and the return from exile.

topics.title: The Return of the Jewish Exiles to Judah

passage_rules.label: Return from Babylon and restoration of Jerusalem's temple

historical_context.setting: Return from Babylonian exile to Judah under Persian imperial administration, culminating in temple restoration.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: The broader return corridor is relevant here, so Logos retains the Babylon–Jerusalem route rather than using only the local Yehud map.
historical_context.source_basis: Bible Atlas chapter 13: Cyrus, Persian Empire, return to Judah, and post-exilic Palestine.

topics.title: The Conquests of Cyrus the Great
The Return of the Jewish Exiles to Judah

historical_context.approximate_date: Traditionally placed in the 5th century BCE
historical_context.setting: Jerusalem and the restored Judean community under Persian rule.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: The local administrative and communal setting is more relevant than the full exile-return corridor.
historical_context.source_basis: Bible Atlas chapter 13: Judah in the Persian period and Palestine after the Exile.

historical_context.setting: Jerusalem during rebuilding, administrative reform, and covenant renewal under Persian imperial rule.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: Jerusalem is emphasized, with neighboring provinces shown to clarify the regional political setting.
historical_context.source_basis: Bible Atlas chapter 13, especially Judah in the 5th century BCE.

passage_rules.label: Post-exilic Judah and Jerusalem under Persian rule

historical_context.approximate_date: Commonly situated in the post-exilic Persian era; exact date uncertain
historical_context.setting: The restored temple community in Judah/Jerusalem.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: The map gives the post-exilic geographic frame without pretending that a precise year can be derived from the book itself.
historical_context.source_basis: Bible Atlas chapter 13: Persian-period Judah and post-exilic Palestine.

passage_rules.label: Late kingdom of Judah under Babylonian pressure

historical_context.setting: Judah and Jerusalem amid Egyptian and especially Babylonian imperial pressure before Jerusalem's fall.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: The map emphasizes Judah, Jerusalem, and surrounding powers rather than later return-from-exile geography.
historical_context.source_basis: Bible Atlas chapter 11: Judah amid international powers.

topics.title: The Rise of the Neo-Babylonian Empire

passage_rules.label: Fall of Jerusalem, displacement, and Babylonian exile

historical_context.setting: Judah after Jerusalem's fall, with displacement toward Babylon and Egypt.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: The wider exile geography is necessary here because the narrative extends beyond Jerusalem.

passage_rules.label: Judean exile in Babylonia with Jerusalem as the theological point of reference

historical_context.setting: Judean exiles in Babylonia, while Ezekiel's visions repeatedly engage Jerusalem and the temple.
historical_context.exegetical_focus: The map keeps both Babylon and Jerusalem visible because the book's geography is deliberately diasporic and Jerusalem-oriented.
